messages:
Alex: quick heads-up — saw a steady memory growth on qwen-mistral when running long-context workloads (48k+ tokens). pmap shows a ~1.2GB drift over ~90m, not reclaimed after evictions :thinking_face:
Maria: ugh. which node / kernel? any evict logs?
Alex: worker-23, kernel=compact_kv_v1 fallback -> compact_kv_v2 selected a few times. eviction logs show frequent small-page frees but total slab usage climbs. attached mini dump in thread.
Sanjay: can you paste the exact repro command? want to run locally.
Alex: sure — quick repro (single-client):
```bash
python serve_bench.py --model qwen-7b --rope-scale 1.0 --seq-len 49152 --batch 1 --duration 5400 --enable-kv-paging
```
Alex: observed pattern: KV allocation spikes aligned with kernel-switch points and when rope-scale crosses 2048 boundary, then small-page fragmentation increases.
Jamie: interesting. I remember earlier we had a compaction threshold tuned for llama/gqa but not for mqa patterns. could be different page churn semantics.
Nina: any perf profiles? flamegraphs?
perf-bot: flamegraph uploaded: https://perf.internal/runs/5102468000/flame.svg (shows heavy time in kv_free()/kv_coalesce). :mag:
Maria: thanks — looking. the flame shows a lot of time in slab allocator during GC/evict. fragmentation ratio ~0.68 in snapshots Alex provided.
Sanjay: hypothesis: kernel selection switching to compact_kv_v2 leads to suboptimal page sizes for MQA models (qwen), leaving many half-full subpages that aren't merged because compaction is rare.
Jamie: two quick experiments: 1) force kernel=compact_kv_v1 for longseq and measure memory drift, 2) increase compaction frequency (kv_compact_interval=30s) and see if reclaim improves.
Alex: ran #1 — forcing v1 reduced drift by ~60% over same run. #2 I haven't tried yet.
Maria: that suggests kernel heuristics are picking v2 because of short-term throughput gains, but long-term reuse is worse. patch idea: bias kernel selection by projected prefix reuse (if long-context workload high -> prefer compact allocation).
Sanjay: also try changing batching heuristic: when batch size is 1 on longseq, prefer smaller kernel working set to reduce fragmentation.
Nina: can we instrument per-kernel fragmentation metrics (free-run-length histogram) and emit to console/trace? would help confirm.
Alex: I'll add a quick metric: kv.fragmentation.histo with buckets (0-0.1, 0.1-0.25, 0.25-0.5, 0.5-1.0) and run another long job.
perf-bot: scheduled perf snapshot job 5102468000-1 at +20m.
Maria: follow-up plan: 1) Alex add histo + run, 2) Jamie test compaction interval change + forcing v1, 3) Sanjay prototype selection bias based on rope-scale and long-prefix ratio. assign owners?
Alex: taking #1, will post logs and pmap deltas.
Jamie: taking #2, will do A/B on dedicated vs hosted.
Sanjay: taking #3, will put a small patch behind a flag and gather canary telemetry.
Nina: add an eval script to exercise GQA vs MQA vs Llama token patterns — want to see model-specific delta.
Alex: quick note — saw a corner where rope-scale 2.0 -> 2.1 boundary triggered double-kernel-change in one request path, causing transient overalloc then async free that didn't compact. logging that separately.
Maria: OK good thread. if we replicate we'll open a perf regression bug and propose kernel-bias flag for next rollout. :thumbsup:
